briefings.title: DeepMind Chief Demis Hassabis Says Google’s Still Winning AI Talent | Semafor Tech
briefings.tldr: Despite escalating industry competition and high-profile departures, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis remains confident in Google's leading research bench and its multi-pronged, simulation-based path toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).

briefings.tldr: Artificial intelligence is driving a monumental shift toward "science at digital speed," enabling researchers to bypass decades of manual labor through computational breakthroughs like AlphaFold.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis On What AI Will Do Next
briefings.tldr: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis projects that AI could help cure all diseases within the next 10 to 20 years by utilizing a suite of "AlphaFold-level" models, while advanced AI tools like "Co-Scientist" are beginning to transition science toward closed-loop automated physical discovery.

briefings.title: A new era of discovery: AI and the frontiers of science with Demis Hassabis
briefings.tldr: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis predicts that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) will arrive between 2029 and 2031, ushering in a transformative "singularity" era marked by self-improving code, agentic systems, and a massive 100x acceleration of scientific and medical discovery.

briefings.title: Why the US Must Engage China on AI Safety Before It’s ‘Game Over’ | Trumponomics
briefings.tldr: The United States must engage China in high-level AI safety negotiations to prevent the global proliferation of dangerous, open-source models, as private corporate governance is insufficient to manage frontier risks like cyber-hacking and bioweapons.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis on AGI, Robots Scale Production, and Elon’s $1T Mars-Shot Comp | EP 253
briefings.tldr: At a special Moonshots panel at MIT, Peter H. Diamandis and exponential technology experts analyzed the rapid scaling of humanoid robotics, the legal battle over OpenAI's corporate governance, and a future where AI-driven scientific discovery and advanced biotechnology reshape global economics and human biology.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis: We're Three Quarters of the Way to AGI
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis views AGI as a 20-year mission on track for completion by 2030, shifting AI’s role from a sophisticated tool to a foundational "language" capable of solving grand scientific challenges in biology, chemistry, and physics.

briefings.title: How to Build the Future: Demis Hassabis
briefings.tldr: AGI is likely achievable by 2030 through the refinement of current architectures and 1-2 remaining breakthroughs in memory and reasoning; the most immediate, defensible opportunities for founders lie in "Deep Tech" where AI intersects with physical sciences and complex search spaces.

briefings.title: (APRIL 27, 2026) BLUE HOUSE BRIEFING
briefings.tldr: President Lee Jae-myung and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis established a strategic partnership centered on the opening of the world’s first "Google AI Campus" in Seoul and collaborative R&D for the "K-Moonshot Project," while projecting the emergence of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) by 2030.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis Wants to Build AGI. Should We Trust Him?
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning founder of DeepMind, is driven by a unique blend of scientific rigor and "spiritual" ambition to build AGI, balancing a high-stakes rivalry with OpenAI against his desire to remain a "good" steward of humanity's most powerful invention.

briefings.title: CFR Fellows' Book Launch Series: The Infinity Machine

people.name: Sebastian Mallaby

briefings.tldr: Sebastian Mallaby’s The Infinity Machine chronicles the rise of Demis Hassabis and DeepMind, illustrating how the pursuit of superintelligence evolved from a niche scientific obsession into a high-stakes commercial and geopolitical arms race.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis: Why AGI is Bigger than the Industrial Revolution & Where Are The Bottlenecks in AI
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis (Co-Founder & CEO of Google DeepMind) predicts AGI—defined as a system matching all human cognitive capabilities—will likely arrive within the next five years, ushering in a shift ten times the magnitude and speed of the Industrial Revolution.

briefings.title: The Hardest Problem AI Ever Solved, with Google DeepMind CEO
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, outlines a future where AI transcends chatbots to become the ultimate scientific tool, moving from solving specific "grand challenges" like protein folding to achieving Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) capable of unlocking "root-node" solutions for human health, energy, and the nature of reality.

briefings.title: The God Machine Demis Hassabis and the Quest for Superintelligence | Sebastian Mallaby
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis is driven by a quasi-spiritual compulsion to advance science through Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), transitioning from a "singleton" vision of safe, collaborative development to a high-stakes competitive arms race against OpenAI.

briefings.title: AI Research Symposium: keynotes by Ashwini Vaishnaw, Demis Hassabis, Yoshua Bengio & Yann LeCun
briefings.tldr: The AI Research Symposium highlighted India’s emergence as a primary global hub for AI adoption and research, with industry leaders predicting the arrival of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) within 5–8 years.

briefings.title: Demis Hassabis On AGI, Advice For Indian Engineers, AI In Gaming & More
briefings.tldr: Demis Hassabis highlights how AI is transitioning from digital assistants to physical-world discovery, potentially compressing drug development timelines from years to weeks while evolving into a "general" intelligence capable of scientific breakthroughs like General Relativity.

briefings.title: The day after AGI: Two 'rock stars' of AI on what it will mean for humanity
briefings.tldr: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is projected to reach human-level cognitive performance as early as 2026–2027, driven by AI systems "closing the loop" to automate their own coding and research.

briefings.title: Google’s AI boss made OpenAI issue code red. Now he wants to solve disease. | Titans and Disruptors
briefings.tldr: Sir Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind and Nobel laureate, is leading a strategic pivot to transform AI from a research endeavor into a "shipping engine" that aims to solve all human diseases and usher in a "new Renaissance" of radical abundance within the next 15 years.

briefings.title: AlphaGenome author roundtable
briefings.tldr: AlphaGenome is Google DeepMind's new AI model, published in "Nature," that unifies DNA sequence-to-function prediction, representing a significant step towards deciphering the entire genome.
